To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in detached tobacco leaves standing in the dark, yellowing is accompanied by a climacteric rise in respiration and in adenylate charge, and that the glycolytic intermediaries between triose phospholates and 3-P-glycerate rise, and those between 3-P-glyerate and PEP fall.
(a) during the yellowing process of detached leaves, the ATP level and adenylate energy charge increase and (b) the glycolytic metabolites fructose 2,6-bisphosphate and pyruvates are elevated.

the rise in respiration rate in the detached leaf is associated with an increase in ATP level and energy-charge, and that this is accompanied by an increase in glycolytic metabolite levels, particularly pyruvate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolic regulation in the senescing tobacco leaf.
the regulation of the glycolytic pathway in tobacco leaves during the senescence process.
the regulation of metabolism in the aging leaf.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the yellowing leaf has an increased capacity to produce ATP, but is not able to use it effectively for biosynthetic processes.
the metabolic events in senescing tobacco leaves are complex and not yet fully understood.
in the detached leaf the glycolytic system is activated by the climacteric, but the mechanism is complex and the details remain to be elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in senescing leaves the adenylate energy charge and glycolytic flux are increased, but the glycolytic metabolite concentrations remain largely constant, with the possible exception of the fructose diphosphatase reaction.
the yellowing leaf is characterized by a rise in respiration rate, a rise in the energy status of the adenylates, and a shift in glycolysis from the oxidative to the fermentative pathway.
the yellowing of detached tobacco leaves is accompanied by a large and rapid rise in the rate of glycolysis, and that this is associated with a rise in adenylate energy charge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the yellowing leaf is a useful model for the study of metabolic regulation.

the yellowing process is associated with a strong climacteric-like rise in respiration, and that this is accompanied by a rise in the adenylate energy charge, a rise in the level of glycolytic metabolites between glucose 1-P and triose phosphatase, and a rise in pyruvates.
the metabolic changes in senescing tobacco leaf can be explained by the operation of known enzymes in the glycolytic pathway.
